body: Yemen's Houthi movement says it has targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile, just a day after the airport partially resumed operations following weeks of disruption. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed in a statement on X on 26 October that the group launched a ballistic missile at the airport and carried out drone attacks against pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's strategic East-West pipeline, saying the attacks achieved their intended objectives; at the time of publishing, the claims had not been independently verified.

Saudi Arabia said its air defences successfully intercepted the latest attack. Saudi military spokesperson Turki Al-Malki said a Houthi ballistic missile bound for Riyadh had been destroyed and confirmed Saudi forces had subsequently carried out strikes against missile launchers and storage facilities inside Yemen. Before the reopening, Saree had warned airlines, airport employees and passengers not to use the facility, describing it as unsafe and a military target, and said the Houthis would continue striking the airport.

King Khalid International Airport had partially reopened on 25 October, with limited domestic flights and selected international services operated by Saudi carriers; under the phased reopening plan, Terminal 1 has been designated for domestic services, while Terminal 2 is handling international flights operated by national airlines. Despite the reopening, flight activity remains significantly below normal levels: according to airline data experts Cirium, the airport has seen 86% of scheduled flights cancelled since 8 October, with 4,071 of 4,736 scheduled services withdrawn. Several international carriers have continued to suspend operations to Riyadh, operational restrictions remain in force under NOTAM A3650/26 and A3651/26, and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency has advised operators to avoid designated areas of Saudi airspace while the US Federal Aviation Administration has warned carriers of military activity and potential interference with satellite navigation systems. According to reports, the airport has been targeted around 20 times since the beginning of October. In light of the attacks, Saudi startup carrier Riyadh Air has confirmed it is temporarily transferring passenger operations to Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Al Qassim, with flights serving Cairo, Dhaka, Jeddah, London Heathrow, Lahore and Islamabad operating from Al Qassim until further notice.
en.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement says it targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile a day after the airport partially reopened; Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted the missile, while flight activity remains far below normal and Riyadh Air is shifting operations to Al Qassim.
en.title: Riyadh airport targeted by Houthi ballistic missile one day after partial reopening

body: 葉門胡塞武裝表示，已以彈道飛彈攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯首都利雅德的哈立德國王國際機場，時間就在機場在中斷數週後部分恢復營運的隔天。胡塞武裝軍事發言人葉海亞·薩雷10月26日在社群平台上宣稱，該組織向機場發射彈道飛彈，並以無人機攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯東西向管線沿線的抽水站，稱攻擊已達成預定目標；但在報導刊出時，這些說法尚未獲得獨立查證。
沙烏地阿拉伯方面表示，防空系統已成功攔截這次攻擊。沙烏地軍事發言人圖爾基·馬爾基表示，1枚飛往利雅德的胡塞彈道飛彈已被摧毀，沙烏地部隊隨後也對葉門境內的飛彈發射器與儲存設施發動攻擊。在機場重新開放前，薩雷曾警告航空公司、機場員工與旅客不要使用該機場，稱其不安全且是軍事目標，並表示胡塞武裝將繼續攻擊機場。

哈立德國王國際機場已於10月25日部分重新開放，營運有限的國內線與部分由沙烏地本國航空公司執飛的國際線；依分階段重開計畫，第1航廈負責國內線，第2航廈負責本國航空公司執飛的國際線。儘管已經重開，航班量仍遠低於正常水準：根據航空數據機構睿思譽的資料，自10月8日以來機場已有86%的排定航班取消，4736班排定航班中有4071班取消。多家國際航空公司仍暫停利雅德航線，飛航公告限制仍在實施，歐盟航空安全局已建議業者避開沙烏地空域的特定區域，美國聯邦航空總署也警告業者注意軍事活動與衛星導航系統可能受到的干擾。據報導，自10月初以來機場已遭攻擊約20次。受攻擊影響，沙烏地新創航空公司利雅德航空已確認暫時把客運業務轉移至蓋西姆的納伊夫·本·阿卜杜勒阿齊茲親王國際機場，往返開羅、達卡、吉達、倫敦希斯洛、拉合爾與伊斯蘭馬巴德的航班在另行通知前均改由蓋西姆出發。
zh.summary: 葉門胡塞武裝表示在機場部分重開隔天以彈道飛彈攻擊利雅德哈立德國王國際機場；沙烏地表示防空系統已攔截飛彈，機場航班量仍遠低於正常水準，利雅德航空已把業務轉移至蓋西姆。
zh.title: 利雅德機場在部分重開隔天再遭胡塞彈道飛彈攻擊
